title: What The Bouzouki Knows (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 104bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal Greek philosophy absurdist Mediterranean Perth
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The bouzouki has a sound that travels faster than the ferry
Between the islands of the Aegean — it's contrary
To the laws of acoustic physics but it doesn't seem to care
The bouzouki makes a sound that's already there when you get there

[Pre-Chorus]
I heard a bouzouki in a taverna in the nineteen eighties
And I haven't quite recovered and the memory never fades

[Chorus]
What does the bouzouki know that I don't know?
It knows the Mediterranean is not a place — it's a tempo and a flow
What does the bouzouki know at two in the morning?
It knows that the best things happen after the usual warning
Has been given and ignored — that's my boy

[Verse 2]
The rebetiko tradition grew from the Greek and Turkish borderland
Where music carried grief across a border nobody planned
The bouzouki was the vessel for the things that couldn't be said
By any means available except the music thread

[Bridge]
There's an Australian-Greek community in Fremantle on the waterfront
Where the bouzouki sounds on Saturday and nobody will confront
The paradox of a Mediterranean instrument beside the Indian Ocean
Because the bouzouki knows that distance is not an obstacle to devotion

[Outro]
Bouzouki knows… the Mediterranean in any longitude… bouzouki knows
That's my boy
